verdict.rationale: Homebrew's Cellar model installs each formula version once and symlinks it into the prefix (homebrew-docs-28), which does mean a given dependency version isn't duplicated per-project like node_modules-style tools — supporting the 'stored once' half of the story. However, there is no evidence of a true content-addressable (hash-keyed) store like Nix/pnpm; kegs are organized by formula name+version, not content hash, and community commentary explicitly contrasts Homebrew unfavorably with Nix's reproducibility/content-addressing model (homebrew-comm-13, homebrew-comm-15). Missing for 10: documentation of hash-based addressing/deduplication, evidence of content-addressable store paths, and independent confirmation that identical content is deduplicated across differing package names/versions.
